quotes.text: Silo tools are great at telling you something happened. They're terrible at telling you what happened in which order across domains. Sequence is the detection.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sums up why correlated incident timelines beat separate point tools.

quotes.text: Everything clicked for me when I realized we aren't under resourced, we're over-fragmented. You don't need another console. You need one incident graph that understands relationships.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes the security staffing problem as a fragmentation problem.

quotes.text: The mailbox is quiet, but the attacker is now living on OAuth. Quarantine isn't containment, it's house cleaning after the thief left with your badge.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Shows why quarantining a phishing mail does not end an intrusion.

quotes.text: Good, except it's a gate, not a cleanup crew. If the tokens are already minted, policy changes are future-facing, the mess is present tense.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains the limits of Conditional Access once tokens are already stolen.

quotes.text: You don't solve identity by yelling at users about MFA. You solve it by collapsing identity, device, and app into one narrative
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the episode's identity fusion argument in one line.

chapters.title: Hybrid security is not more tools
Blind spot 4: Cloud apps and shadow IT

takeaways: Siloed email, identity, endpoint and cloud app tools each see only part of an attack, so the correlation work lands on analysts and dwell time grows.
Defender XDR fuses these signals into one incident timeline and can revoke tokens, kill sessions, remove OAuth consents, roll back mailbox rules and isolate devices from one place.
Response order matters: cut identity and SaaS persistence before or alongside device cleanup, or reinfection loops continue.
hook: Six dashboards and three vendors still leave four blind spots that attackers live in: email, identities, endpoints and cloud apps. This episode shows security teams in hybrid Microsoft environments how Defender XDR turns scattered alerts into one incident story with cross-domain response, and why consolidation pays back.
